mechanics: Grid-based incremental: spores generated per second by placed mushrooms
Basic Shrooms generate 1 spore per second
Fever Shrooms make adjacent mushrooms generate 2x spores, stacking
Radio Shrooms increase the range of mushrooms with area effects
Shy Shrooms generate 10 spores per second but none if adjacent to another mushroom
Pop Shrooms generate 1 per second but fire the pop effect 10 times when popped
Every second each mushroom has a 10 percent chance to become poppable and highlight yellow; clicking pays its spore amount times 10
Each type costs 10 spores at base, doubling for each further one of that type
Right click or long press deletes a mushroom and halves that types cost
Supports 8 players at a time with claimable plots assigned on joining
Shroom inventory bar at the bottom of the screen showing every type and its current cost
Select then click a grid square to place, or drag from the button onto the grid
Mushrooms bounce slightly while active, and grow elastically before springing back when popped
Spore output shown over a mushroom on hover or when the player is near
Classic blocky Roblox aesthetic
vfx and sfx on every interaction - hover, click, place, pop, UI
notes: Adjacency is the whole game - Fever doubles neighbours, Shy fails next to anyone, Radio extends range - so the grid must be a true 8 by 8 lattice of equal cells rather than a decorative checkerboard. tile-grid carries the request but not the adjacency requirement.
Preset Sandbox taken on its own plot-isolated shape, which matches the eight claimable plots. Its social-hub is carried through unused because the shop is screen UI rather than a place.

Stage B was close. Every interaction is a click or drag on screen, which points at SET, but players have avatars, are assigned plots and have billboards in front of them, so the space is treated as walked on and SET was not added.

notes_for_us: tile-grid is filed under Strategy and Party and Casual and reads as a trivia floor or a board, but it is the only row in the system for a placement lattice - which is the entire map for grid builders like this one. Simulation cannot see it without loading the whole option catalogue.
Cell size and grid dimensions are load-bearing here, and count is a free-text string on one pick, so 8x8 and 4x4x4 survive only as words. Nothing downstream can act on them as numbers.
Stage B does not really answer a game where the space is walkable but every interaction is a click. SET is described as geometry nobody walks on, and this is geometry people walk on but never touch.
